artworks.title: The Artemision Bronze
artworks.description: Monumental ancient Greek bronze recovered from a shipwreck off Cape Artemision, now in the National Archaeological Museum, Athens. The god strides forward with his arm drawn back to hurl a weapon now lost — a thunderbolt if he is Zeus, a trident if Poseidon — making it one of the finest surviving bronzes of the Severe style.

artworks.title: The Statue of Zeus at Olympia (reconstruction)
artworks.description: Plate from Antoine-Chrysostome Quatremère de Quincy's study Le Jupiter olympien, reconstructing the lost gold-and-ivory Statue of Zeus at Olympia. Phidias's colossus, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, showed the god enthroned with a figure of Nike in his right hand and a sceptre in his left.

artworks.title: Jupiter and Thetis
artworks.description: Oil painting by Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres, now in the Musée Granet, Aix-en-Provence. The sea-nymph Thetis caresses the chin of the colossal, enthroned Jupiter as she pleads for the fortunes of her son Achilles, a scene drawn from the first book of the Iliad.

artworks.title: Jupiter and Io
artworks.description: Oil painting by Antonio da Correggio from his series on the loves of Jupiter, now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna. The god, dissolved into a dark cloud from which a face and hand barely emerge, embraces the nymph Io — one of the most sensuous inventions of Renaissance painting.

films.title: Clash of the Titans
films.description: Ray Harryhausen's stop-motion Olympus puts Zeus at the board of the gods, releasing the Kraken with a chess-piece gesture — the modern template for a cinematic king of the gods.

films.title: Hercules
films.description: Disney's gospel Olympus casts Zeus as a booming, affectionate father whose infant son is stolen from the cradle — for a generation, the first face of the king of the gods.

films.title: Jason and the Argonauts
films.description: Harryhausen's adventure opens on Olympus, where Zeus and Hera wager on Jason's voyage; the gods lean over the mortal board like players at a game.

popCulture.title: God of War III
popCulture.creator: Santa Monica Studio
popCulture.description: The climax of the Greek God of War trilogy sends Kratos up Mount Olympus to kill Zeus himself — the father-son feud rewritten as a siege of the gods.

popCulture.title: Hades
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Supergiant's underworld roguelike keeps Zeus on the surface as a booming Olympian relative whose boons crackle into Zagreus' runs — the king of the gods as a voice in the ear.
